source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #286 (branch fix/282-ref-is-null-tail at head 91dd280f3c81d03cc7ee3fb3b88f8d806166d4af — branch commit d3005b1 (restore tail dispatch in op_ref_is_null (#282)) plus merge commit 91dd280 bringing in current main 94a0eca, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45206926698 and 45206945651 against the branch and pull-request run 45206866309, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #286 (#282, op_ref_is_null has the same non-tail dispatch as op_f64_const: the #240 identity barrier in crates/telomere/src/runtime/vm/refs.rs is replaced with the volatile-load form proven in #277, restoring the handler's tail dispatch). The branch merged current main (94a0eca, containing PR #287) before measurement; the only conflict was in crates/telomere/tests/call_threading.rs, where both sides had appended a same-shaped loop test at the same location (main's f64.const test from #277 and this branch's ref.is_null test), resolved by keeping both tests. After the merge the op_ref_is_null replacement is present exactly once, the only remaining black_box barrier is op_return's intentional exception, and a full disassembly audit of the merged tree shows 261 TAIL / 1 NONTAIL among the named barrier handlers (the only NONTAIL being op_return), with op_ref_is_null verified TAIL by direct disassembly. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (94a0eca) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45206965424, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. 18 of the 32 gated series change, all by ±16 B except one at −32 B: in release, stripped file grows by +16 B in core, component, core-aot, core-nosimd, wasi and wasi-threads, and stripped .text is unchanged everywhere; in release-size, stripped file shrinks by −16 B in component, core, core-aot, core-nosimd and wasi and by −32 B in wasi-threads, grows by +16 B in core-jit, and stripped .text shrinks by −16 B in component, core, core-aot, core-nosimd and wasi-threads. The baseline configuration is byte-identical in both profiles. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.47% (1,169,031 B to 1,232,983 B), unchanged from +5.47%. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
